paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: how you treat people shows what your faith is really doing. James says as we hold out our faith in our glorious Lord Jesus Christ, we are not to show favoritism (James 2:1). Giving the best seat to the man with the gold ring and telling the poor man to stand means we have "become judges with evil thoughts" (James 2:4). I know I'd be the shabby one in that room, so this one hits close to home.

Now here's what makes favoritism so serious. James says God has chosen the poor of this world to be rich in faith and to inherit the kingdom He promised those who love Him (James 2:5). The royal law is "Love your neighbor as yourself," and if you really fulfill it, you are doing well (James 2:8). But if you show favoritism, you sin and are convicted by the law as transgressors (James 2:9). And James won't let us shrug it off as a small slip, because whoever stumbles at just one point is guilty of breaking all of it (James 2:10).

So what do we do with that? We speak and act as those who are going to be judged by the law that gives freedom (James 2:12). James says "judgment without mercy will be shown to anyone who has not been merciful. Mercy triumphs over judgment" (James 2:13). Baker, that means the person in front of you gets the same welcome no matter what they're wearing, and we get to pass along the mercy we've been given. Go be generous with it, because the oven's got room for EVERYBODY!
